text:
Beckett Sennecke's breakout is on hold. The Ducks placed him on injured reserve with an upper-body injury before Saturday's game in Utah, after he had already missed the Nov. 17 game in St. Louis, so he has sat out three of Anaheim's last four. He left behind 12 goals and 26 points in 22 games at age 20, in his second season.

For perspective: forwards picked in the top five since 2005 scored a median 0.54 points a game in their first full season. He's at 1.18. Anaheim had given him 20:16 a night and 82% of its power-play chances, and our form check called his recent run earned, since the Ducks were creating more with him on (18.2 on-ice expected goals over ten games against 14.4 usual).

The luck is the caution. Anaheim has scored 11.0 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and he's shooting 22.6% against a talent we put near 14%. Evolving-Hockey had his team generating chances at a 97th-percentile rate with him out there last season, though opponents got more too. Watch for his return, then the shooting.
